title: Beyond screens: Mercedes-Benz's new holographic heads-up display
gist: Mercedes-Benz is prototyping a holographic display that uses holographic optical elements in film laminated into the windshield as a possible successor to HUDs and passenger screens, at a time when its executives say screens are not luxury. The prototype's resolution beats current HUDs but is far behind touchscreens, and it is unclear whether customers want it.

insights.claim: Luxury automakers face the question of what comes after screens, because luxury features trickle down to mainstream cars and screens can only get so big.

insights.so_what: If the luxury premium shifts to craftsmanship, interior-materials suppliers gain and display-heavy differentiation loses value.

insights.claim: Mercedes' holographic display pairs a projector with a transparent film laminated into the windshield that contains holographic optical elements, or 'super-small mirrors', which reflect light selectively so the image stays visible in direct sunlight while hidden from the driver.
